text.arabic_uthmani: قَالَ إِن سَأَلْتُكَ عَن شَىْءٍۭ بَعْدَهَا فَلَا تُصَٰحِبْنِى ۖ قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِن لَّدُنِّى عُذْرًۭا

baseline.text: Musa, Bundan sonra sana bir şey sorarsam artık bana arkadaşlık etme. Artık benden yana geçerli bir özrün var, dedi.

findings.text: Musa bir sonraki soruyu arkadaşlığın bitiş şartı yaparak kendi tekrarlanan başarısızlığına usule bağlı bir sınır koyar; sınıra varılınca ilişkinin durumu değişecektir.

activation_trace.role: Negotiated speech makes the utterance function as an agreed relational term.
Questioning or requesting supplies the precise act that will activate the term.
Temporal succession fixes the term to the next question after the present breach.
Companionship as continued attendance is the relation explicitly placed at stake.
Arrival at an endpoint presents the justification as already complete rather than merely offered.
Doing enough to become excused gives the companion standing to end the association.

changed_reading.after: A self-authored exit clause: one more question will make separation justified by the speaker's own concession.
changed_reading.before: A renewed apology and promise not to question again.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The conditional "if I ask you about anything after this" is joined directly to "do not accompany me" and to the completed reaching of an excuse.
baseline_models.mechanism: The speaker converts one future question into a publicly legible termination event. Speech negotiates the term, the temporal marker fixes its next activation, and the reached excuse transfers justification for ending companionship to the addressee.

activation_trace.role: Reaching an endpoint anchors the focus excuse as a completed threshold.
Excuse achieved by sufficient action names what has matured at this relational threshold.
The vowed arrival supplies the journey's first explicit destination pattern.
Gathering separated elements makes the first destination a conjunction against which later parting stands out.
Actual arrival confirms that reaching language records crossed thresholds, not aspiration alone.
The orphans' future arrival extends the threshold pattern into protected maturation.
Attaining full strength specifies the later endpoint as one that must be allowed to ripen.

changed_reading.after: The journey has reached another kind of destination: the meeting-point quest becomes a separation threshold, with later protected maturity warning against forcing an endpoint before its time.
changed_reading.before: The companion has simply accumulated enough reason to leave.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated reaching links unlike endpoints: the sought confluence, its actual arrival, the focus excuse, and the orphans' maturity. The focus clause therefore marks a relational threshold within a journey structured by arrivals, while the later maturity threshold shows that not every endpoint should be forced early.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated reaching at a confluence, an excuse, and maturity; I infer a shared threshold grammar and a contrast between joining and parting. A live alternative is ordinary lexical repetition without a designed relational sequence.
structural_cues: The same reaching root occurs at 18:60, 18:61, 18:76, and 18:82.
The uncited ل د ن echo runs from knowledge "from Us" at 18:65 to excuse "from me" at 18:76, but the packet supplies no branch inventory for it.

activation_trace.role: The act of asking anchors the breach as a demand for an account.
The general knowable object marks an action treated as already available for settled report.
Holding oneself back supplies the required posture toward an unresolved action.
Complete cognitive encompassment names what the questioner presently lacks.
Knowledge of an affair's interior supplies the hidden layer unavailable at first sight.
Following behind makes temporal deference part of companionship.
The guide's own bringing-forth of the matter reserves disclosure initiative to him.
Articulated mention defines the awaited verbal account that questioning anticipates.

changed_reading.after: The speaker recognizes that his questions repeatedly demand a finished account of a still-unfolding thing before the guide has chosen to disclose its interior.
changed_reading.before: The speaker promises to suppress further curiosity.

context_deltas.mechanism: Following requires bearing an action whose inner account is not yet encompassed and waiting until the guide initiates disclosure. The focus question is thus not neutral curiosity; it is pressure to turn an unresolved thing into an immediate report before its explanatory time.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a knowledge deficit, required restraint, and guide-initiated mention; I infer that premature questioning forces the timing of disclosure. A live alternative is that asking matters only as disobedience, irrespective of epistemic timing.
structural_cues: 18:67-70 ties failed patience to incomplete interior knowledge and explicitly makes mention speaker-timed.
The objections at 18:71 and 18:74 judge visible acts before the explanations at 18:79-82 disclose their deferred relations.

activation_trace.role: Excuse and removal of blame anchor the transfer of exculpatory standing.
Continued attendance is the obligation from which the addressee is released.
Accountability for fault supplies the earlier claim the speaker asked to have suspended.
Loss of recollection supplies the first breach's mitigating ground.
The repeated failure to hold back shows that the mitigating allowance has not repaired the pattern.

changed_reading.after: He concedes that his conduct has already furnished the guide an excuse, waiving any complaint when companionship is ended.
changed_reading.before: He offers the guide another excuse for his own conduct.

context_deltas.mechanism: After the first objection, the speaker asks not to be held for forgetfulness; after the second, the warning about failed patience returns. The focus excuse therefore reverses the earlier plea: instead of seeking release from accountability, he now grants the companion release from any obligation to continue.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an earlier mitigation plea and a repeated patience failure; I infer that the first allowance has been consumed and the focus statement waives any claim to continued company. A live alternative is escalating apology without a juridical transfer.
structural_cues: 18:73 asks for non-accountability and ease after the first objection.
18:75 repeats the forecast of failed patience after the second objection immediately before the focus concession.

activation_trace.role: Companionship as sustained attendance identifies the mode that the condition will close.
Distinguishing and separating the two parties explicitly executes the focus boundary.
A delivered report begins the explanatory mode at the moment of parting.
Return to an affair's outcome supplies the retrospective content promised after separation.
The final return to outcomes closes the explanatory phase opened at parting.

changed_reading.after: One more question closes learning-by-accompaniment but simultaneously opens learning-by-retrospective interpretation.
changed_reading.before: One more question simply forfeits further teaching.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next objection executes the focus condition, but parting is immediately paired with promised report and interpretation. The threshold ends participatory companionship while opening retrospective explanation; loss of company is therefore a change of pedagogical mode, not simple cancellation of all instruction.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the direct sequence from third question to parting to report; I infer a pedagogical phase transition from participation to retrospective interpretation. A live alternative is actual expulsion followed only by a final courtesy explanation.
structural_cues: The third objection at 18:77 is followed directly by parting and a promise to explain at 18:78.
Ayat 18:79-82 deliver the explanations only after embodied companionship has ended.

remaining_uncertainties: The repeated ب ل غ sequence may be thematic thresholding or ordinary lexical recurrence.
The waiver reading is functionally coherent but more juridical than the surface grammar requires.
The extraction outlier must remain an analogy and must not be rendered as etymology.
strongest_changes: The clause is a self-authored exit term rather than only an apology.
Questioning becomes a timing error produced by judging without interior knowledge.
Separation closes accompaniment but opens retrospective interpretation.
summary.what_was_special: The strongest latent activation came from the repeated reaching thresholds and from the packet's split س ء ل -> س ل ل mapping, which permits a contained image of questioning as premature extraction.

activation_trace.role: Gentle or hidden drawing-out recasts the focus question as extracting concealed explanation.
The same mapped extraction image sharpens the prior ban as a ban on drawing the account out early.
The guide's own act of bringing the matter forth contrasts voluntary disclosure with extraction.
The later delivered report shows the concealed account eventually emerging on the guide's initiative.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, each question pulls a hidden account from its sheath before the guide releases it, and the final pull tears the companionship while eliciting the report.
changed_reading.before: Asking is a prohibited request for information.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a form-distant split-root activation, not a lexical claim about سأل. It remains valid because the packet explicitly maps the focus root to س ل ل and the reading stays anchored to the focus question; downstream prose should present it only as an exploratory material analogy for drawing out an explanation before voluntary disclosure.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus verb "I ask you" is the act that will end companionship.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The learner converts repeated failure into a boundary condition.** `ب ل غ` B001 (“reaching the limit”) makes the teacher reach an excuse from Moses himself. This echoes geographic and maturational limits elsewhere (18:60, 82, 86, 93): once reached, the relation changes state. I infer that Moses authorizes termination to restore integrity to the apprenticeship’s rule. His speech creates accountability through a self-imposed endpoint.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:78 showed the self-imposed limit working: the next question ends companionship and releases interpretation.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Excuse as a procedural limit reached.** `ع ذ ر/B004` is going far enough to be excused; `ع ذ ر/B001` is claiming or receiving excuse. Moses converts the next question into a termination condition; 18:77 triggers it, 18:78 announces separation, and 18:79–81 supplies interpretations only after the allowance is exhausted. I infer that `عُذْرًا` belongs to a measured process, not merely interpersonal pardon. The teacher has reached the point at which ending companionship can itself be justified.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:77 triggered the agreed limit, 18:78 separated the companions, and 18:79–81 made explanation the teacher’s final justified act.

words.gloss_range: completed speech act introducing Musa's self-imposed condition and concession
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) opens the ayah as a completed speech turn: Musa is carried by the 3ms verb without being renamed, so the focus falls on the concession he now voices. The speech is not neutral narration; it externalizes a judgment into a binding rule. In the Musa-al-Khidr dialogue chain, this new {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) answers the earlier warnings in 18:72 and 18:75 and reprises the pact shape of 18:70, but now the student formulates the consequence against himself. The opening word therefore frames the whole quoted utterance as condition, prohibition, and justification.
words.root_gloss_range: root range of saying, speech, declaration, and held opinion; local use selects outward declaration that makes an inner judgment binding

topics.headline: completed declared concession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Musa's concession is voiced as a completed declaration, not left as an inner realization or loose narration.
topics.reason: The perfect Form I speech verb introduces the full quoted conditional utterance, and the local discourse supports a declared self-imposed consequence.

topics.headline: speaker carried by morphology
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar bridges from the prior exchange into Musa's new condition without spending a separate noun on speaker identification.
topics.reason: The verb carries 3ms agreement with no overt subject, so the identity is supplied by dialogue continuity.

topics.headline: dialogue pact reprise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this speech turn is a reversal of the earlier asking-ban pact in 18:70 and an answer to the repeated warning formula in 18:72 and 18:75.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL inter-ayah rows give concrete same-surah references, and the local quoted structure indeed reprises condition and prohibition language.

topics.headline: utterance architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first word governs a structured legal-like utterance: condition, consequence, then reason.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the whole following sequence as quoted content with conditional protasis, apodosis, and explanatory clause.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle opening a contingent self-test whose result is the prohibition clause
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) begins the self-imposed test and holds the future breach as contingent rather than certain. Because it is followed by the perfect {{ar:سَأَلْتُكَ}} ({{tr:sa'altuka}}), the possible future asking is imagined as already completed if it happens. The particle also echoes the conditional pact of 18:70, reversing the direction: al-Khidr once set the condition for Musa's following, and Musa now sets the condition for his own dismissal.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: perfect asking verb inside the conditional protasis

topics.headline: conditional self-test scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dismissal is framed as a conditional rule, not as an immediate rupture or a prediction.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks words 2-6 as the protasis and words 7-9 as the apodosis.

topics.headline: completed hypothetical force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices Musa speaking of a possible future question with the grammar of completed occurrence, intensifying the self-accusing tone.
topics.reason: The conditional particle is followed by a perfect verb in the protasis, matching the CRITICAL aspect claim.

topics.headline: earlier pact echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the reprise of the earlier condition in 18:70, now tightened into Musa's own self-dismissal clause.
topics.reason: The same-surah echo is concrete and fits the local condition-plus-result structure.

words.gloss_range: asking or questioning addressed directly to al-Khidr, locally functioning as the possible breach-channel
words.prose: {{ar:سَأَلْتُكَ}} ({{tr:sa'altuka}}) carries the whole breach in one verb: Musa is the first-person asker, al-Khidr is attached as the second-person object, and {{ar:عَنْ شَيْءٍ}} ({{tr:ʿan shay'in}}) supplies the matter asked about. The perfect form inside the condition makes any later question feel already attributable to Musa if it occurs. Lexically the root field moves beyond neutral curiosity toward a demand for explanation, which is exactly what the pact in 18:70 had barred. The internal hamza gives the asking verb an audible catch, matching the interruption that another question would cause. The word therefore turns asking into the trigger that puts companionship at risk.
words.root_gloss_range: root range of asking, questioning, requesting, and demanding; local structure selects renewed inquiry as a demand that can end companionship

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prepositional topic phrase naming the matter asked about

topics.headline: argument-complete asking
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices both sides of the strained relation packed into the verb: Musa asks, al-Khidr is the one asked, and the topic follows separately.
topics.reason: The verb has first-person subject agreement, a second-person object suffix, and a governed prepositional topic.

topics.headline: completed future breach
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the self-accusing force of treating a possible later question as grammatically complete.
topics.reason: The protasis uses a perfect 1s verb after the conditional particle.

topics.headline: asking as demand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the forbidden act is not mere curiosity but a renewed explanatory demand placed on al-Khidr.
topics.reason: The local dismissal frame selects the questioning/demand side of the root range.

topics.headline: asking pact reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Musa internalizes the earlier do-not-ask rule of 18:70 and makes his own asking the instrument of separation.
topics.reason: The same root and governed topic frame recur from the earlier pact, with the direction now reversed.

topics.headline: asking trigger structure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the asking verb is the pivot from possible breach to immediate result, binding inquiry to loss of companionship.
topics.reason: The verb is the predicate of the protasis whose result is the prohibition against companionship.

topics.headline: hamza catch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an audible catch inside the asking verb that suits the interruption caused by another question.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation is local texture, not an independent grammar claim.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the topic of inquiry, with aboutness selected locally
words.prose: {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}) keeps the grammar clean: al-Khidr is the person asked through the suffix on {{ar:سَأَلْتُكَ}} ({{tr:sa'altuka}}), while {{ar:شَيْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay'in}}) is only the matter asked about. The preposition makes the next noun an intellectual target rather than a second direct object. Its away-from range remains only a secondary color, suiting the relational strain without displacing aboutness. It also repeats the exact about-anything frame of 18:70, so Musa's condition sounds like a citation of the original restriction.

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: asking verb with the addressee attached as object
indefinite matter governed by the preposition

topics.headline: topic of inquiry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition separates the person questioned from the matter questioned about.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the prepositional phrase as the topic complement of the asking verb.

topics.headline: aboutness with separation color
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices aboutness doing the main grammatical work while the preposition's away-from range lightly suits the relational strain.
topics.reason: The local construction selects inquiry-aboutness; separation is retained only as secondary semantic coloring, not as the governed sense.

topics.headline: pact phrase repetition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the governed phrase repeats the earlier forbidden topic-frame of 18:70.
topics.reason: The same prepositional frame is explicitly tied to the concrete earlier pact reference.

words.gloss_range: indefinite genitive matter or thing, locally broad enough for any possible inquiry topic
words.prose: {{ar:شَيْءٍ}} ({{tr:shay'in}}) makes the condition maximally broad: not a named issue, not a class of issues, but any single thing or matter after this point. Its wide Quranic profile as thing or matter supports hearing it as the widest possible object of questioning here. Its genitive case comes from {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}), so it is the topic of inquiry, not a second direct object. The singular indefinite form means one future matter would be enough. The same noun repeats the scope of the earlier ban in 18:70, while its tanwin also balances the final indefinite {{ar:عُذْرًا}} ({{tr:ʿudhran}}): an open trigger is answered by a sufficient but unnamed justification.

words.gloss_range: keep me as companion or accompany me, locally reciprocal companionship under prohibition
words.prose: {{ar:تُصَٰحِبْنِى}} ({{tr:tuṣāḥibnī}}) names the relationship that would end: al-Khidr is the second-person subject, Musa is attached as the first-person object, and the jussive form makes continued companionship stoppable by prohibition. The local sense is not mere walking beside someone; Form III keeps mutual companionship and pedagogical engagement in view. Variant readings test simpler accompaniment, causative agency, and stronger prohibition, but the received surface preserves reciprocal companionship as the marked choice. The emphatic ṣ, guttural ḥ, long ā, and final ī make the relationship linger in sound just as the text makes it conditional. The companion-root is mostly nominal elsewhere, so this finite Form III makes companion-status into an action that can collapse after the failed patience exposed in 18:75.

words.gloss_range: you have reached or attained, locally reaching a sufficient excuse rather than arriving at a place
words.prose: {{ar:بَلَغْتَ}} ({{tr:balaghta}}) transfers reaching language from travel into moral-relational limit. The second-person perfect assigns the completed threshold to al-Khidr: Musa says you have reached an excuse from my side, not I have reached my limit. The object {{ar:عُذْرًا}} ({{tr:ʿudhran}}) and the source phrase {{ar:مِنْ لَدُنِّي}} ({{tr:min ladunnī}}) narrow the root away from physical arrival and toward sufficient justification. This fits the wider Sūrat al-Kahf reaching motif, including 18:60, 18:86, and 18:93, but here the destination is the limit of companionship. The final ghayn gives the reaching verb guttural weight at the threshold defined by the prior incapacity in 18:75.

words.prose: {{ar:عُذْرًا}} ({{tr:ʿudhran}}) is the word the ayah lands on. Grammatically it can be heard as the reached object or as a specification of the reaching, and {{ar:مِنْ لَدُنِّي}} ({{tr:min ladunnī}}) can qualify it as an excuse from Musa's own side. Its terminal position, rare gerund profile, and echo of the excuse-warning pairing in 77:6 make the ending feel like an earned justification rather than a decorative close.
